trip.name: Rhône River Cruise, Lyon to Arles (fictional)

destinations.name: Lyon
facts: In 1895 the Lumière brothers filmed workers leaving their Lyon factory: one of the first films ever shown.
The Jacquard loom, which weaves patterns with punched cards, was perfected in Lyon in 1804, and is an ancestor of the computer.
Lyon has more than 400 "traboules", hidden passages that silk workers used to carry cloth through the old city.

destinations.name: Tournon
facts: Valrhona chocolate has been made across the river from Tournon since 1922.
The Vivarais steam train climbs through the Doux gorges on a line built in the 1890s.

destinations.name: Viviers
facts: Viviers is one of the smallest cities in France with its own cathedral.
Pétanque was born in 1907 in La Ciotat, a few hours south: the name means "feet together" in Provençal.

destinations.name: Avignon
facts: Seven popes lived in Avignon between 1309 and 1377, and the Palais des Papes is the largest Gothic palace in the world.
Châteauneuf-du-Pape wines may be blended from up to thirteen grape varieties.
The Pont du Gard, 49 metres high, carried water to Nîmes for about 500 years.

destinations.name: Arles
facts: Van Gogh painted about 300 works in Arles in just fifteen months.
The Roman amphitheatre of Arles, built around 90 AD, still holds bullfights and concerts for some 20,000 people.

options.name: Old Lyon Walking Tour
options.difficulty_note: More than 200 steps. A gentle walking group is also offered.
options.description: Coach up to Fourvière, then a guided walk down through Old Lyon: Basilica of Notre-Dame de Fourvière (inside and out), the Roman Ancient Theatre, a panoramic viewpoint, the Jardin du Rosaire, the Saint-Jean district and at least one traboule. Ends with a pink praline tasting.
options.accessibility: More than 200 steps on the walk down; a gentle walking group is also offered.

options.name: Silk Experience at Maison des Canuts & Mur des Canuts
options.difficulty_note: No local guide, led by an trip guide.
options.description: Visit of the Maison des Canuts in the Croix-Rousse: live weaving demonstration on a Jacquard hand loom, plus the museum and film on the history of silk and silkworms. Groups swap halfway. Group photo at the Mur des Canuts mural on the way back.

options.name: Bike Tour of Lyon & Parc de la Tête d'Or
options.difficulty_note: Minimum age 14. Bikes provided by the ship's wellness host.
options.description: About 1.5 hours of biking with local guides from the riverfront to the Parc de la Tête d'Or, through the park with photo and story stops, and back toward the ship through the city.

options.name: Flavors of Lyon: Food & Wine Tour
options.difficulty_note: If there is a second coach, it does the same tour in reverse order (Halles first, Vieux Lyon second).
options.description: Culinary walk in Vieux Lyon with tastings (praline brioche, chocolate), then Les Halles de Lyon Paul Bocuse: the story of Paul Bocuse and three tasting stops (charcuterie with red wine, cheeses with white wine, macaron), followed by free time in the market. Junior guest version with milder tastings and no wine.

options.name: Beaujolais Vineyard Tour & Tasting
options.difficulty_note: Junior guests have their own program with an trip guide: juice tasting, small sandwiches and outdoor games.
options.description: Scenic drive into the Beaujolais, then Château des Ravatys: welcome and story of the estate, a 90-minute tour of the winery, vineyards and courtyard, and a guided tasting of 4 wines with local bread, ham, sausage and cheese. Free time to buy wine at the end.

options.name: Bike Tour of Lyon & Parc de la Tête d'Or
options.difficulty_note: Minimum age 14.
options.description: Same as the morning bike tour: about 1.5 hours from the riverfront to the Parc de la Tête d'Or and back through the city.

options.name: Steam Train (Train de l'Ardèche / Vivarais Railway)
options.difficulty_note: No local guide. Open-air cars, or closed cars if the weather requires it.
options.description: Private steam train departure at 10:00 from Tournon Saint-Jean station, about 25 minutes up the Doux gorge to Colombier-le-Vieux, where the locomotive is turned, then back to Tournon. Commentary by the trip guides. Free time at the station for souvenirs and photos before the coach back.
options.accessibility: Open-air train cars, or closed cars if the weather requires it.

options.name: Chapel Hike & Cité du Chocolat (Valrhona)
options.difficulty_note: No local guide on the hike. Closed-toe shoes required for the chocolate workshops.
options.description: Coach to the top of the Hermitage hill, leisurely hike down through the vineyards, then the Cité du Chocolat in Tain-l'Hermitage: 'From Bean to Bar' tasting workshop on Valrhona Grand Crus and a self-guided visit of the chocolate museum. Junior guests do a guided museum visit and a chocolate pop (lollipop) or tablet workshop.

options.name: Château de Tournon Visit with Wine Tasting
options.difficulty_note: Lots of steps. Wine purchases cash only. No coach, no local guide.
options.description: Walk from the ship to the Château de Tournon. Wine tasting of 3 local wines led by a Cave de Tain representative, plus a self-guided visit of the château. Groups rotate between the tasting and the visit.
options.accessibility: Lots of steps at the château.

options.name: Viviers Walking Tour with Pétanque
options.difficulty_note: Pétanque capacity 60 guests per hour, groups rotate.
options.description: Guided walk through medieval Viviers (Saint-Vincent Cathedral, Maison des Chevaliers exterior) with stories about local history and culture, plus a 60-minute pétanque discovery game with local players on a court near the ship.

options.name: Université du Vin Wine Tasting & Château de Suze-la-Rousse (adults)
options.difficulty_note: Adults. No local guide.
options.description: One hour by coach to Suze-la-Rousse. Tasting of 6 wines with a wine expert at the Université du Vin, then a short visit of the château and its exhibition on the Drôme wine heritage.

options.name: Château de Suze-la-Rousse Juniors Experience
options.difficulty_note: Family departures only. Accompanied by an trip guide.
options.description: Junior guest program running alongside the adult wine tasting: walk and games in the Garenne natural park among the ruins of the lords of Baux' estate, then a tour of the château with stories about castle life. JAs meet their families at the château entrance.

options.name: Viviers Walking Tour with Pétanque
options.difficulty_note: Pétanque capacity 60 guests per hour.
options.description: Same as the morning tour: guided walk through medieval Viviers plus a 60-minute pétanque game.

options.name: Aven d'Orgnac Cave & Prehistory Museum
options.difficulty_note: Junior cave painting limited to 20, family departures only.
options.description: One hour by coach to the Aven d'Orgnac. Guided walk through the cave (Joly, Chaos and Red chambers), exit by elevator, plus a self-guided visit of the Prehistory museum with audioguides. Junior guests do a cave painting workshop instead of the museum (natural pigments, twig brushes). Groups rotate 14:15 to 16:45.

options.name: Université du Vin Wine Tasting & Château de Suze-la-Rousse (adults)
options.difficulty_note: Adults.
options.description: Same as the morning tour: 6-wine tasting at the Université du Vin and a short château visit.

options.name: Château de Suze-la-Rousse Juniors Experience
options.difficulty_note: Family departures only.
options.description: Same as the morning Junior program: park walk with games and château tour.

options.name: Artistic Luberon: Roussillon & Ochre Paths
options.difficulty_note: Lunch on own, 12:45 to 15:00.
options.description: One hour by coach to Roussillon. Painting workshop making your own paint from natural ochre pigments, a walk on the introductory part of the Ochre Path, a short guided walk of the village, then lunch and free time in Roussillon on your own.

options.name: Pont du Gard I: Kayaking from Collias to the Pont du Gard
options.difficulty_note: Minimum age 6, must be able to swim, not for pregnant women. No flip-flops. No towels or changing rooms. Second coach 15 minutes later (07:30 to 12:30). Can be cancelled by the supplier in bad weather.
options.description: Coach to Collias, safety briefing and equipment, then about 2.5 hours kayaking down the Gardon river with local guides, ending under the Pont du Gard.

options.name: Pont du Gard II: Museum & VIP Access
options.difficulty_note: VIP walk has 80+ stairs, not accessible; museum-only option available. Lunch choices made on Day 1.
options.description: Self-guided visit of the Pont du Gard museum and a VIP guided walk across the top level of the aqueduct (groups of 30, about 45 minutes each), followed by a 3-course seated lunch at Les Terrasses du Pont du Gard.
options.accessibility: The VIP walk has more than 80 stairs and is not step-free; a museum-only option is available.

options.name: Lavender Workshop & Museum
options.difficulty_note: No local guide on the coach.
options.description: Guided visit of the Lavender Museum on the history of lavender growing in Provence, a lavender sachet making workshop, and a tasting of at least 4 lavender-infused products (honey, tea, biscuits...). Free time in the garden and shop.

options.name: Châteauneuf-du-Pape Wine Tasting
options.difficulty_note: Two groups of up to 45 rotate between visit and tasting.
options.description: Visit of the vineyard and cellar at Domaine Mousset with an English-speaking guide, and a tasting of 3 wines with light snacks. Junior guests get sweet non-alcoholic drinks.

options.name: Avignon Walking Tour with Palais des Papes
options.description: Guided walk from the ship: Pont Saint-Bénézet (the bridge of Avignon), Notre-Dame des Doms cathedral, a 60-minute guided visit of the Palais des Papes, and some free time in town.

options.name: Avignon Late Riser: City Overview & Bakery Stop
options.description: Gentler, later walk in small groups: city orientation, the Place du Palais (exterior of the Palais des Papes and cathedral), and Les Halles market with a local pastry and a hot drink, plus about 15 minutes to explore the market.

options.name: Arles Introduction Tour
options.difficulty_note: Optional, guests can also explore on their own or stay on the ship.
options.description: Guided evening walk in Arles from the ship: the Roman amphitheatre, the Van Gogh garden at the Hôtel-Dieu and other monuments, with some free time.

options.name: Van Gogh: Saint-Paul de Mausole & Painting Workshop
options.difficulty_note: If there is a second coach, it does the two parts in reverse order.
options.description: One hour by coach to Saint-Rémy-de-Provence. A Van Gogh-inspired painting workshop and a guided visit of the Saint-Paul de Mausole monastery, where Van Gogh stayed and painted.

options.name: Les Baux-de-Provence & Carrières des Lumières
options.difficulty_note: Cobbled, steep streets, good walking shoes.
options.description: Immersive digital art show in the Carrières des Lumières, an old limestone quarry at the foot of Les Baux, then free time to walk the hilltop village of Les Baux-de-Provence.
options.accessibility: Cobbled, steep streets: good walking shoes.

options.name: Moulin du Calanquet Olive Mill
options.difficulty_note: Second coach if needed: 09:30 to 12:00.
options.description: Guided walk in the olive groves, visit of the mill and how olive oil is made, guided tasting of the estate's award-winning olive oils, then free tasting of olives, tapenades, jams and mustards, and shopping.

options.name: Les Baux-de-Provence & Carrières des Lumières
options.difficulty_note: Cobbled, steep streets, good walking shoes.
options.description: Guided walk of the village of Les Baux-de-Provence with a local expert (groups of up to 25), then the immersive art show at the Carrières des Lumières.
options.accessibility: Cobbled, steep streets: good walking shoes.

options.name: Moulin du Calanquet Olive Mill
options.difficulty_note: Second coach if needed: 15:00 to 17:30.
options.description: Same as the morning visit: olive grove walk, mill visit, olive oil tasting and shopping.
